report.summary: Parsed chunk 2 of reach.py: _Src dataclass, source scanning helpers, import splitting, dispatch chain detection, and toplevel name binding. Verified claims against visible code.

handoff.purpose: Define internal helper types and functions for scanning Python source files to extract import records, dispatch chains, and module-level bindings.

symbols.name: _Src
symbols.note: Dataclass for mutable scratch data of one parsed module. Fields: rel, dotted, tree, records, func_records, func_names, func_calls, func_loops, dispatch, has_main_guard, is_shim, literals, dynamic, dyn_targets, weak, toplevel.

symbols.name: _py_dotted
symbols.note: Converts a relative file path (e.g., 'dir/mod.py') to a dotted module name (e.g., 'dir.mod') by stripping '.py' and replacing '/' with '.'.

symbols.name: _iter_py
symbols.note: Walks a root directory recursively, collecting all .py file paths relative to root, sorted.

symbols.name: _walk
symbols.note: Wrapper around os.walk that filters out ignored directories (those in _IGNORE_DIRS or starting with '.'), yields sorted dirnames and filenames.

symbols.name: _is_main_guard
symbols.note: Returns True if an AST node is an if statement with test '__name__ == "__main__"'.

symbols.name: _branch_literals
symbols.note: Extracts string literals from a branch condition (Compare, BoolOp, or startswith/endswith call). Returns list of strings.

symbols.name: _dispatch_chains
symbols.note: Finds flat if/elif chains inside a function AST, returns list of chains where each chain is list of (literal, node) pairs, only if chain length >= _MIN_DISPATCH_BRANCHES.

symbols.name: _DEAD_BRANCH
symbols.note: String constant 'inside a branch that can never run (`if False:`)'.

symbols.name: _SUPPRESSED
symbols.note: String constant 'inside a `try:` whose ImportError is swallowed'.

symbols.name: _is_never_true
symbols.note: Returns True if test is a constant with falsy value (e.g., False, 0).

symbols.name: _catches_import_error
symbols.note: Returns True if a try node has a handler that catches ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError.

symbols.name: _split_imports
symbols.note: Returns (live, weak) tuple of import records from a subtree, considering dead branches and suppressed imports.

symbols.name: _import_records_of
symbols.note: Returns only live import records from a subtree, ignoring weak ones.

symbols.name: _toplevel_names
symbols.note: Returns set of names bound at module level (import time), descending into if/try/with up to depth 3.

symbols.name: _module_level_bindings
symbols.note: Returns dict mapping names to list of import records for module-level imports. Only processes top-level Import/ImportFrom statements.

symbols.name: _shim_body
symbols.note: Returns True if module body consists only of imports, __all__, and plain alias assignments (no def/class/executable statements).

claims.text: Mutable scratch for one parsed module. Never escapes ``analyse``.
claims.why: The claim about never escaping 'analyse' refers to a function not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Covers the two shapes real dispatch chains use: ``x == "literal"`` and ``x.startswith("/api/")`` (web_api routes a prefix on several paths). A branch we cannot read contributes nothing rather than a guess.
claims.why: Code handles Compare (including x == literal), BoolOp (recursively), and Call with startswith/endswith. Unrecognized branches return empty list per docstring intent.

claims.text: A chain is only a command table when it is long enough (``_MIN_DISPATCH_BRANCHES``); shorter ones are ordinary conditionals and reporting them as subcommands would fabricate entry points.
claims.why: The constant _MIN_DISPATCH_BRANCHES is not defined in this chunk; its value cannot be verified.

claims.text: ``if False:`` / ``if 0:`` -- a branch the interpreter deletes. Deliberately literal-only. Inferring that some NAME is falsy would make the walk guess, and a guess in this direction silently deletes real edges.
claims.why: Function checks if test is ast.Constant and not truthy. Only literal constants, no name inference.

claims.text: Does this ``try`` swallow a failing import? Narrow on purpose: only handlers that NAME ImportError (or ModuleNotFoundError) count. A bare ``except Exception`` around an import is usually a lazy-optional-dependency idiom too, but widening this rule reclassifies real edges on evidence that is not there.
claims.why: Code checks handler type names (ast.Name or ast.Attribute) against _IMPORT_ERRORS tuple. Bare except Exception is ignored.

claims.text: Structural descent rather than ``ast.walk`` because the whole point is the CONTEXT an import sits in: the same statement is evidence in one branch and not in another.
claims.why: Function uses recursive descent (rec inner function) instead of ast.walk, processing children based on context (if, try).

claims.text: LIVE import records only. Weak ones are reachable only via :func:`_split_imports`, so no caller can pick them up by accident.
claims.why: Function returns only first element of _split_imports result (live records). Weak records are discarded.

claims.text: Names a module binds at import time. Descends one level into ``if`` and ``try`` because conditional definitions are ordinary in this codebase.
claims.why: Function handles if, try, with, asyncwith up to depth 3 (not just one level as doc says, but doc says 'one level' which is ambiguous; code descends up to depth 3, but claim about descending into if/try is accurate).

claims.text: ``from .projects import resolve_repo_root`` binds ``resolve_repo_root`` to the projects MODULE for reachability purposes: referencing that name inside a dispatch branch is a real dependency on that module, and it is how HTTP route handlers reach anything at all (they call ``hierarchy.hierarchy``, never ``import hierarchy`` inside the branch).
claims.why: The example and behavior about dispatch branches and HTTP route handlers refer to code outside this chunk.

claims.text: MODULE LEVEL ONLY, and that restriction is load-bearing. cli.py's branches all write ``from .doctor import main as m`` / ``from .benchmark import main as m`` -- the SAME local name ``m`` in sixty different branches. Binding names from every scope made ``m`` resolve to all sixty modules, so every subcommand appeared to reach every other subcommand's target and the whole dispatch collapsed into one blob. A branch's own imports are handled separately, from that branch's own records.
claims.why: The example and reasoning about cli.py and dispatch branches refer to code outside this chunk.

claims.text: True when the module body re-exports and does nothing else. Detected structurally, never guessed: no def, no class, no executable statement beyond imports, ``__all__`` and plain alias assignments. A shim is worth naming because it is the one module class where "nothing reaches it" is expected rather than alarming.
claims.why: The function body is incomplete in this chunk (starts but is truncated). The full implementation cannot be verified. However, the beginning shows it checks for first element being an Expr with Constant (likely docstring), and the claim about structural detection is plausible but uncheckable.
